title: Find the Town Judge
summary: In a town with n people labeled from 1 to n, determine if there is a town judge.
statement: In a town with n people labeled from 1 to n, determine if there is a town judge. The town judge trusts no one, and everyone else trusts the town judge. There is exactly one person who meets these criteria. Given an array of trust relationships, where each element trust[i] = [ai, bi] indicates that person ai trusts person bi, return the label of the town judge if one exists, or return -1 if the town judge cannot be identified.
constraints: The judge trusts nobody and is trusted by every other person.
Return the judge label, or -1 when none exists.
hints: Net score indegree-outdegree equals n-1 only for a judge.
Subtract one from truster and add one to trusted person.
Return the label with score n-1, otherwise -1.
Reaching n-1 requires all n-1 incoming edges and zero outgoing edges under distinct trust pairs.
editorial: Reaching n-1 requires all n-1 incoming edges and zero outgoing edges under distinct trust pairs.

tests.explanation: Person two has incoming trust from everyone else and no outgoing trust.
Person three trusts one, so no town judge exists.
